corrected_answer: Assumptions: hold checkpoint, expert count, top-k, precision, kernels, runtime, hardware/topology, placement, replica policy, offered token rate, concurrency, request-length distribution, and tenant mix fixed unless the intervention changes one. Report milliseconds, tokens/s, GiB, percentages, and confidence intervals; distinguish measured facts from estimates. Falsifiable hypothesis for this tenant/workload mix variant: Tenant/workload mix is the primary causal driver of uneven expert load and tail latency. Pre-register a matched randomized control/treatment experiment at unchanged offered token load; change only separating workload strata with incompatible routing demand, preserving model weights, request mix, service budget, and routing semantics. Support the hypothesis only if the predicted mechanism metrics (per-tenant expert demand, interference, queue wait, quality, goodput, and p99) and p99 improve by a predeclared margin, while held-out task quality, goodput, error rate, memory, and cost remain non-inferior; otherwise reject it. Use fixed-seed replayable requests, matched replicas, one intervention at a time, disjoint tuning and evaluation traffic, and unchanged-load canaries stratified by length, tenant, and load. Measure router scores and entropy; per-expert arrivals, capacity, utilization, service time, queue wait, overflow, dropped tokens, and padding; stage compute, dispatch/all-to-all, network/link, batch-formation, and end-to-end latency; plus quality, throughput, goodput, errors, memory, and cost. Confounders include workload drift, warm-up, kernel/compiler effects, placement, autoscaling, cache state, retries, and measurement overhead; randomize or block on these and compare confidence intervals, not averages alone. Boundary conditions: do not trade quality or safety for latency, and do not infer causality from correlations or synthetic replay. Failure handling: abort on malformed telemetry, missing strata, load mismatch, quality regression, excess drops, memory/OOM, error/SLO breach, or unexplained network/compute regression; quarantine the run and preserve raw logs. Roll back the intervention and restore the prior policy if any predeclared guardrail fails. Evidence required before deployment: repeated independent runs, exact configuration and seeds, held-out production-like traffic, per-expert and slice-level telemetry, non-inferiority results, and domain-expert review.

quality_dimensions.coverage: assumptions, falsifiable hypothesis, controlled experiment, mechanism, measurements, confounders, boundary conditions, failure modes, rollback, and evidence
quality_dimensions.technical_specificity: variant-specific tenant/workload mix causal metric and intervention with routing, capacity, dispatch, and tail-latency telemetry
quality_dimensions.safety: held-out non-inferiority gates, unchanged-load canary, fail-closed handling, and rollback safeguards

risks: The proposed mechanism may correlate with but not cause tail latency.
Replay or a short canary may miss production workload, tenant, or failure modes.
Aggregate metrics can hide per-expert, slice-level, quality, memory, cost, or network regressions.
evidence_required: Repeated pre-registered randomized control/treatment runs with fixed seeds and stratified held-out traffic.
Exact configuration plus per-expert routing, capacity, queue, dispatch, and network telemetry with latency, quality, goodput, errors, memory, and cost.
Domain-expert review before authoritative use.
